page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-lc1m2.large is a shared, burstable virtual instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache. Compute capacity is delivered via one physical core structured into two burstable vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, supporting modern vector instruction sets including AVX and AVX-512F alongside AES hardware encryption.

The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes zero bundled local storage, necessitating reliance on remote block storage solutions for disk operations, and has a baseline network bandwidth profile listed at 0 Gbps. Accelerated graphics hardware is absent, with GPU count standing at zero.

Benchmark measurements place the instance within the lowest decile across compute, memory, and throughput evaluations. Stress-ng returned 922.69 for single-core and 1862.68 for multi-core compute throughput, while Geekbench recorded a single-core score of 721.0 and a multi-core score of 1191.0. Large-block uncached memory read and write operations operated at 14.22 GB/sec and 13.09 GB/sec respectively. Application-level metrics demonstrate low execution rates, achieving 0.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 0.43 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its shared hypervisor resource model, burstable processing constraints, and baseline performance ceilings, ecs.t5-lc1m2.large functions as an entry-tier budget instance. It is technically suitable for lightweight background services, low-traffic web hosting, basic test environments, and non-critical utility automation tasks that experience intermittent utilization cycles.
